plates.title: The Book of Bugs
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript page, vellum-toned, gold leaf edges on every framed vignette, fine red-ink ribbons linking the scenes, in the hand of a medieval bestiary illustrator painting small mechanical creatures instead of animals. Top of page: a large illuminated capital scene of a robed scholar at a writing-desk throwing up his hands as a small tape-creature on the desk misbehaves, titled MY PROGRAM DID THE WRONG THING. Below, three scenes side by side, linked downward by ribbon from the first: on the left a tape-machine with a reading head over a strip of 0s and 1s with a wrong 9 scrawled where an 8 should be, titled OUTPUTS 9 INSTEAD OF 8; in the middle two scribes comparing mismatched copies of the same scroll, titled TWO COPIES, ONE BUG; on the right a row of painted doubling cells that scatter into a broken pattern at the fourteenth cell, titled BREAKS AT FOURTEEN. These three ribbons converge downward into two more scenes: a monk pulling back a woven pattern to reveal a simpler nested pattern beneath, titled THE PATTERN BENEATH THE PATTERN, and a cartographer's hand tracing branching paths on a map that all dead-end, titled NO PROOF IS FOUND. Both ribbons tie into a central knot held by a hooded figure, titled THE KNOT THAT MUST BE PULLED — this is the page's hub, drawn larger than the rest. From the knot, four ribbons fan outward and down to four scenes arranged in a row: a tester with a tally-stick counting successes unaware of a hidden failure off his ledger, titled DID I TEST ENOUGH CASES; a traveler recoiling as a tangled thicket grows past a simple gate, titled SOME TYPICAL SURPRISES; a mathematician's carved number-tablets with one anomalous '2' among a row of 1s, titled A COEFFICIENT OF TWO; a smith forging well-fitted tools at an anvil beside scattered rough fragments, titled LANGUAGE DESIGN IS KEY. All four ribbons gather at the bottom into one final scene: the opening scholar now smiling at his tape-creature, with a ribbon looping back up to the top of the page, titled A SUCCESS, NOT A FAILURE. Palette: aged parchment cream, iron-gall brown ink linework, muted gold, deep red and blue pigment accents. No lettering anywhere except the short capitalized titles beneath each framed vignette.

vignettes.quote: for input 7, there’s a bug! Instead of outputting 7 + 1 = 8, the Turing machine outputs 9

vignettes.title: OUTPUTS 9 INSTEAD OF 8

vignettes.quote: if a compiler optimizer changes what a program does, then it’s a bug
vignettes.depicts: Two scribes copying the same scroll into different hands, one holding up his copy against the other's and frowning at a mismatched line.
vignettes.title: TWO COPIES, ONE BUG

vignettes.quote: suddenly there’s a “bug”—like here at n = 14
vignettes.depicts: A row of painted cells doubling neatly in size, then at the fourteenth cell suddenly scattering into a wrong, broken pattern.
vignettes.title: BREAKS AT FOURTEEN

vignettes.quote: it’s exactly the rule 122 elementary cellular automaton
vignettes.depicts: A monk pulling back the edge of a complicated woven pattern to reveal a simpler nested pattern underneath, like rule 122.
vignettes.title: THE PATTERN BENEATH THE PATTERN

vignettes.quote: our inability to know in general what a program will do except in effect by explicitly running it
vignettes.depicts: At the page's center, all the ribbons from the machine-scenes and the proof-scenes are tied into a single knotted cord held by a hooded figure who only knows the knot's shape by pulling it taut.
vignettes.title: THE KNOT THAT MUST BE PULLED

vignettes.quote: Did I Test Enough Cases? The Failure of Ruliological Induction
vignettes.depicts: A tester with a tally-stick counting many identical successful trials, unaware of one hidden failing case just off the edge of his ledger.
vignettes.title: DID I TEST ENOUGH CASES

vignettes.quote: Some Typical Ruliological Surprises
vignettes.depicts: A traveler peering through a simple gate and recoiling as an unexpectedly tangled thicket grows up on the other side.
vignettes.title: SOME TYPICAL SURPRISES

vignettes.quote: you try x105 – 1. And suddenly there’s something different—a coefficient of 2
vignettes.depicts: A mathematician's tablet of clean carved numbers, with one tablet further down the row bearing an anomalous carved '2' where all the rest show only 1s.
vignettes.title: A COEFFICIENT OF TWO

vignettes.quote: Language design, I believe, is key.
vignettes.depicts: A smith forging well-shaped tools on an anvil, each tool fitting a worker's hand exactly, in contrast to the scattered rough tape-fragments nearby.
vignettes.title: LANGUAGE DESIGN IS KEY

vignettes.quote: if we’re doing science, we might consider it a success
vignettes.depicts: At the bottom, the same scholar from the opening scene now smiling at his wayward tape-creature, a loop of ribbon curling back up to the first vignette.
vignettes.title: A SUCCESS, NOT A FAILURE

plates.title: Where the Bugs Were Caught
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript page, vellum-toned, gold-edged frames, fine brown-ink ribbons chaining the scenes top to bottom, in the hand of a medieval bestiary illustrator painting small mechanical tape-creatures instead of animals. Open with the overview's desk-scholar bent over a tape-machine writing 'n+1' with satisfaction, titled IT SEEMS TO COMPUTE N PLUS ONE. Below it, the same machine's head scratches a wrong 9 onto a tape strip ending in three 1s, titled AT SEVEN, THE MACHINE SCRIBBLES A NINE. A ribbon leads to a long unrolled scroll of correct outputs that tears open at its fifteenth mark, titled FLAWLESS UNTIL FIFTEEN, and from there to a grander, many-geared machine whose sixty-third output tile reads 72 instead of 64 after sixty-two perfect trials, titled AT SIXTY-THREE, SEVENTY-TWO APPEARS. Beside these, a cluster of tape-strips ending in unbroken runs of 1s are marked with small red warning flags, titled ALL-ONES TAPES ARE RISKIEST — this begins a second row of scenes. Next, two identical tape-machines running in lockstep suddenly swerve their heads onto different squares at the twenty-seventh step, titled TWO MACHINES PART WAYS AT 27, leading to a row of neat even-numbered output tiles interrupted by one odd 9 at the thirty-second tile, titled AN ODD NINE AMONG EVENS. The plate closes at the bottom with a cellular-automaton pattern of doubling cells breaking apart into a wrong shape at its twenty-fourth step, titled DOUBLING FAILS AT TWENTY-FOUR. Arrange the seven scenes in three loose clusters (tape machines, diverging machines, automaton), each cluster lightly bordered, connected by ribbons flowing downward in the order described. Palette: aged parchment cream, iron-gall brown linework, muted gold, small red accent flags, deep blue tape-markings. No lettering anywhere except the short capitalized titles beneath each framed vignette.

plates.title: Where Proof Succeeds or Fails
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript page, vellum-toned, gold-edged frames, fine brown-ink ribbons chaining scenes top to bottom, in the hand of a medieval bestiary illustrator. Open the plate with the overview's doubling-cell pattern drawn plain and simple, admired by a nodding monk, titled SIMPLE ENOUGH TO TRUST BY EYE. A ribbon leads down to two assistants unrolling a tangled woven pattern across a long table, counting a hundred thousand marks without finding a flaw, titled A HUNDRED THOUSAND TRIALS, NO FLAW. Below, a frustrated timekeeper sets aside his hourglass and tally-sticks to unroll the whole weave directly, titled LOOKING AT THE WHOLE WEAVE, leading to a scholar lifting a corner flap of the weave to reveal a simpler nested pattern hidden beneath, titled THE RULE 122 HIDDEN WITHIN, and then to the same scholar sealing a scroll over the now-complete pattern, titled SEALED: NO BUGS, EVER — this closes the left-hand cluster of 'visual and structural proofs,' lightly bordered together. On the right, begin a second cluster: a scholar at a lectern writing linked symbols and brackets beside a tape-machine, titled A NOTATION FOR THE MACHINE, leading down to the same scholar completing a climbing ladder of symbolic statements that reaches a sealed line at the top, titled A LADDER OF PROOF TO THE TOP. At the very bottom of the page, a different, searching scholar follows the same kind of ladder far further, each rung ending only in blank unfinished parchment, titled THE LADDER NEVER REACHES A PROOF. Palette: aged parchment cream, iron-gall brown linework, muted gold leaf, small deep-blue and red ink accents. No lettering anywhere except the short capitalized titles beneath each framed vignette.

vignettes.quote: simple enough that it’s “visually obvious” that they’ll “correctly double” for all input sizes
vignettes.depicts: Opening the plate, the same doubling-cell pattern from the overview's hub scene, now drawn plain and simple, admired by a monk who nods confidently without needing to check further.
vignettes.title: SIMPLE ENOUGH TO TRUST BY EYE

vignettes.quote: But if we run this case up to n = 100000, no bugs appear
vignettes.depicts: A different, more tangled woven pattern being unrolled by two assistants across a very long table, counting a hundred thousand marks without finding a flaw.
vignettes.title: A HUNDRED THOUSAND TRIALS, NO FLAW

vignettes.quote: It’d be very difficult to see this if one just looked at something like stabilization times
vignettes.depicts: A frustrated timekeeper with an hourglass and tally-marks sets these aside and instead unrolls the whole woven pattern to study it directly.
vignettes.title: LOOKING AT THE WHOLE WEAVE

vignettes.quote: it’s exactly the rule 122 elementary cellular automaton
vignettes.depicts: A scholar lifts a corner flap of the tangled weave to reveal a simpler, nested pattern hidden underneath it, labelled by its familiar shape.
vignettes.title: THE RULE 122 HIDDEN WITHIN

vignettes.quote: the underlying cellular automaton must always correctly “double its input”, with no bugs
vignettes.depicts: The scholar closes a scroll with a satisfied seal, the woven pattern finally shown complete and whole beneath it.
vignettes.title: SEALED: NO BUGS, EVER

vignettes.quote: a notation that can encompass both the behavior of the Turing machine
vignettes.depicts: A second scholar at a lectern writes linked symbols and brackets on a fresh page, building a formal symbolic notation beside the tape-machine it describes.
vignettes.title: A NOTATION FOR THE MACHINE

vignettes.quote: we’ve been able to prove that for all inputs n the machine correctly computes n + 1, with no bugs
vignettes.depicts: The scholar completes a chain of linked symbolic statements climbing the page like a ladder, reaching a final sealed line at the top proving the machine correct for every input.
vignettes.title: A LADDER OF PROOF TO THE TOP
